message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have the pink monopoly and $636 cash. I will build houses on those properties.

I need $700 to build seven houses on the pink properties. I will mortgage St. James Place for $90 to cover the shortfall. Then I can build three houses on Virginia, two on States, and two on St. Charles. I will keep Connecticut Avenue unmortgaged as a cash buffer.

I can only perform one action per turn. Building six houses now would leave me with $36 and weaker rent. The three-house spike on Virginia is essential to threaten bankruptcy. I am checking whether p2's dark blues at two houses each pose a serious threat.

p2 has $195 cash. They can mortgage an unmortgaged railroad for $100 to build one more house on a dark blue. A third house on Boardwalk would generate $1400 in rent, which is lethal.

p2 is currently on Virginia Avenue, but they will not pay rent again until they land there again. p3 is at New York Avenue and p4 is at a Chance space. I am at Reading Railroad after mortgaging the B&O.

I am reconsidering keeping Connecticut unmortgaged. After building seven houses, I would have only $26 left. Mortgaging Connecticut for $60 would give me a safer $86 buffer. It would also block p3's light blue monopoly.

Mortgaging Connecticut Avenue will not transfer ownership, so p3 still cannot complete the light blue monopoly. The only downside is losing $8 in rent and paying $66 to unmortgage it later. With only $26 left after building seven houses, I should mortgage Connecticut now for a safer buffer.

I will mortgage St. James Place first to afford the seven houses, then build, and decide on Connecticut afterward. Trading is not viable because p4 rejected offers and giving cash to p2 would be unwise. p3 is weak with only one house on red properties.
